h1: The 6 Best Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combos of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six ergonomic keyboard and mouse combos, sorted by mouse shape, wrist support, connectivity and value.
summary: The Logitech Wave Keys and Lift combo is the best ergonomic keyboard and mouse set: a cushioned wave keyboard with a true vertical mouse. The MX Keys S combo is the premium multi-device pick, and the MEETION is the budget split with a vertical mouse. The cheap wave-key combo with a phone holder gives little mouse relief.
intro: The word ergonomic on a combo box often describes only half the set. A wave-shaped keyboard paired with a conventional flat mouse still twists your forearm every time you reach across the desk, which means the mouse is where most of the strain relief lives. Boxes rarely say so, and a sculpted mouse is not the same thing as a vertical one.

We read six combos from spec sheets and owner reports, then ranked them on how ergonomic the mouse is, how supportive the keyboard is, connection options, battery type and overall value. Two budget combos with weaker ergonomic claims were left out. A premium typing set can land lower than a plainer one if its mouse changes nothing about your wrist.

products.name: Logitech Wave Keys Keyboard & Lift Mouse Ergonomic Combo - Graphite
products.verdict: The only combo here where both the keyboard and the mouse are truly ergonomic.
products.description:
The Logitech Wave Keys and Lift combo pairs a wave-shaped keyboard with a cushioned rest and the Lift, a true vertical mouse. They share a receiver or connect by Bluetooth, and run for months on batteries. A vertical mouse holds the hand in a handshake posture, so the forearm stops twisting, while the wave keyboard curves the rows toward the fingers.

It ranks first because both pieces carry an ergonomic purpose. The MX Keys S set types well but its mouse stays conventional, and the MK670 gives a standard-shaped mouse.

Buy it for heavy daily typing and mousing. The caveats are that the Lift is right handed as sold, with a separate left-handed version, and the keyboard is a wave, not a split. Skip it if you are left handed and want one box.
products.idealFor: Daily heavy typists wanting a complete ergonomic setup.
products.skipIf: You are left handed and want one box.

products.name: Logitech MX Keys S Combo Performance Wireless Keyboard and Mouse - Graphite
products.verdict: A premium typing and mousing set with multi-device switching on both halves.
products.description:
The Logitech MX Keys S combo pairs a low-profile backlit keyboard with a sculpted MX Master-line mouse, connecting through Logi Bolt or Bluetooth with multi-device switching on both halves and a rechargeable battery. Switching between a laptop and a tablet with a key press is a daily convenience for people who work on several devices.

It ranks second because the keyboard is flat and the mouse, though sculpted, is not vertical. The Wave Keys and Lift combo does more for posture at lower cost.

Buy it if you move across devices and want a premium feel. Skip it if you want a vertical mouse or a wave keyboard. The higher price bracket pays for typing quality and flexibility, not for a wrist-friendly angle.
products.skipIf: You want a vertical mouse or wave keyboard.

products.name: MEETION Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse, Wireless Keyboard with Vertical Mouse
products.verdict: A split curved keyboard plus a vertical mouse without a premium bill.
products.description:
The MEETION combo has a split curved keyboard with a wrist rest and a true vertical mouse, connected through a single 2.4GHz USB receiver, with rechargeable parts and Windows and Mac compatibility. A split keyboard straightens the wrists more than a wave, and the combo gets both pieces at a price under $100.

It ranks third because there is a learning curve and no Bluetooth is listed. Brand polish trails Logitech, and the build feels less premium.

Buy it if you are curious about split ergonomics on a budget. Skip it if you need Bluetooth or a premium build. Plan to spend a few days adapting, and keep your old keyboard handy at first.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers curious about split ergonomics.
products.skipIf: You need Bluetooth or premium build.

products.name: Logitech Wave Keys MK670 Combo Wireless Keyboard and Mouse - Graphite
products.verdict: A comfortable wave keyboard with a compact matching mouse and one receiver.
products.description:
The Logitech MK670 combo has a wave keyboard with a cushioned rest and a compact companion mouse, sharing a single USB receiver with a Bluetooth alternative, powered by AA and AAA batteries. A single receiver leaves a port free, and the cushioned wave suits typists who want comfort without retraining.

It ranks fourth because the mouse is a conventional shape, so the forearm still twists, and the disposable batteries need replacing. It costs a bit less than the Wave Keys and Lift.

Buy it if you want wrist comfort on a budget and your mouse use is light. Skip it if you want an ergonomic mouse. For long hours, the Lift in the top-ranked set is worth the upgrade.
products.idealFor: Typists wanting wrist comfort on a budget.

products.name: Logitech MX Keys Combo for Business Keyboard and Mouse - Graphite
products.verdict: MX ergonomics with the fleet management features IT teams ask for.
products.description:
The Logitech MX Keys Combo for Business pairs a low-profile keyboard with a sculpted mouse, using the Logi Bolt secure receiver, fleet management support, multi-device switching and a rechargeable battery. Business management features matter to IT teams buying in bulk, where security and deployment count.

It ranks fifth because those features add cost for personal buyers and the keyboard is flat. It matches the MX Keys S in hardware and adds the admin tools.

Buy it for an IT-managed office buying in quantity. Skip it for personal use, since the MX Keys S gives the same typing feel without the fleet extras. Neither set changes the angle of the wrist.
products.idealFor: IT managed offices buying in bulk.
products.skipIf: You are buying for personal use.

products.name: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Full-Sized Ergonomic Wave Keys with Memory Foam Wrist Rest & Phone Holder
products.verdict: A cheap full size wave keyboard with a thick wrist rest and a phone holder.
products.description:
The budget wave-key combo has a full-size wave keyboard with a memory foam wrist rest, an integrated phone holder, a standard-shape wireless mouse and a 2.4GHz USB receiver. A thick foam rest is soft, and a phone holder is a small convenience.

It ranks last because the mouse is flat and standard, the build is budget, and a thick rest can raise the hands. Next to the MK670, it offers less brand backing.

Buy it for casual wrist comfort at the lowest price. Skip it if you have wrist or forearm pain, because a flat mouse does nothing for the twist. Expect modest relief, not a posture fix.
products.idealFor: Casual users wanting cheap wrist comfort.
products.skipIf: You have wrist or forearm pain.

whatMatters.detail: A vertical mouse holds your hand in a handshake position, which reduces the forearm twist a flat mouse forces. This matters most for people who click for hours each day. Look for the words true vertical in the listing rather than just ergonomic or sculpted. The Lift and the MEETION mouse qualify, while the MX Master line and the others do not.

Wave keyboards curve the key rows to match your fingers, and split designs separate the halves to straighten the wrists. Splits are more ergonomic but take days to learn. Pick a wave if you want comfort with no adjustment period, as with the Wave Keys, and a split like the MEETION if you want a bigger posture change.

A palm rest keeps your wrists from bending upward while you type. Cushioned or memory foam rests feel softer, but a thick rest raises your hands. Check whether the rest is attached and how thick it looks in the product photos. The Wave Keys has an attached cushion, and the budget combo uses memory foam.

A 2.4GHz receiver uses a USB port and is simple to set up. Bluetooth frees the port and pairs with tablets, and multi-device switching changes devices with a key press. Look for the connection types in the title or bullets. The MEETION lists no Bluetooth, while the Logitech sets offer it or Logi Bolt.

Rechargeable sets avoid buying cells, while AA or AAA models run for months and swap instantly. Rechargeable batteries can degrade over years. Check the listing for battery type and runtime before buying. The MX Keys sets and the MEETION recharge, and the Wave Keys and MK670 use disposable cells.

faq.q: Does an ergonomic combo work with Mac?
faq.a: Most do, and the MEETION lists Windows and Mac support. Check the listing for compatibility and for keys like Command before buying, since a Windows-first layout may need remapping, and confirm Bluetooth pairing works on your Mac.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying an ergonomic combo?
faq.a: Choosing a wave keyboard with a flat mouse and expecting relief. The mouse is usually the bigger source of strain, so a set like the Wave Keys and Lift, with a vertical mouse, does more for your wrist than a nicer keyboard alone.

faq.q: Is the Lift mouse worth it over the standard MK670 mouse?
faq.a: For long hours, yes. The vertical shape cuts forearm twist, while the MK670 mouse is a conventional shape. If you click only lightly, the MK670 is enough and costs less, so match the choice to your hours.

faq.q: How long does adjusting to a split keyboard take?
faq.a: Owners usually report a few days to a couple of weeks. Start with short typing sessions, build up gradually, and keep your old keyboard nearby. The MEETION is the split option in this guide.

faq.q: How do I keep a wrist rest clean?
faq.a: Wipe it with a slightly damp cloth and let it dry. Memory foam and cushioned rests collect oils faster than hard plastic, so clean the Wave Keys cushion and the budget foam rest regularly, and let them dry fully.

faq.q: Can left handed users use these?
faq.a: Most mice here are right handed. The Wave Keys and Lift set has a separate left handed Lift mouse, and the vertical MEETION mouse should be checked against its listing before you order.

finalTake: The Logitech Wave Keys and Lift combo is the right ergonomic set for most desks, because both pieces actually change posture. The MX Keys S suits multi-device work, and the MEETION is the cheap split option. Judge the mouse before the keyboard, since that is where the strain starts.
